back: The ceremony of bringing home the spirit of a dead person, held about a year after death, so that it can become an ancestor.
As a transition to the spirit world; the person remains part of the family as an ancestor.
John Mbiti's phrase for ancestors who remain part of the family's life.

front: Why do mourners wash their hands after a burial?
back: Purification: it marks the return to ordinary life.

front: Who prepares the body in a traditional funeral?
back: Close relatives, usually of the same sex as the dead person.

front: Why is kurova guva important to the family?
back: It completes the spirit's passage; a spirit brought home protects the family, while a neglected one is feared to bring misfortune.

front: What does the Constitution (section 80) protect that applies to inheritance?
back: The rights of women, including widows; property grabbing is unlawful.

front: How have funerals changed in recent years?
back: Urban life, Christianity and Islam, burial societies and costs have changed customs; many families combine traditions.
